current.text: He is the projected starting center for Toronto and the only seven-footer on the roster.
The expected closing five is a small, switchable group with Collin Murray-Boyles at center, not Poeltl.
Reports say he is in good shape this summer, and experts said he looked good in early preseason games.

Experts blame his back for last season's drop in blocks and his poor season. They hope the blocks come back and lean optimistic. One speaker is not worried about the back unless it flares up again in training camp.
Experts call his late price too low. He is a good bench flyer, and taking him around pick 130 is a great pick. He is worth a look outside the top 100 if healthy.
If he plays 28 minutes and the back was the reason his blocks dropped, he is an easy top 70 pick.
He went for 4 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
His 70% field goal shooting last season came on low volume and is not expected to last.
He turned only 35% of his deflections into steals last season, so his steals are likely to improve.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs this season and three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games, with a top defense that should hold or improve.

durable.text: He is an elite finisher. His FG% on solid volume is a clear league outlier that lifts a team's FG%.
His free throw shooting has improved steadily. He is no longer a hack target shooting around 52%, but his FT% is still low.
He has lost a step on defense and is not an elite rim protector.
His back flared up repeatedly last season.

note: Both Yahoo and ESPN value him at about 1 USD and rank him 117th, well below the 15 USD he cost in our league last season. Experts see a cheap bench flyer with top 70 upside. He fits punt 3PM builds and gives you a big FG% boost, but costs some FT%. Early in the season, check whether he plays about 28 minutes, whether his blocks come back toward the 1.1 to 1.5 range and whether the back holds up.
